A lake in Cameroon killed 1,700 people in one night, without a sound.
Lake Nyos sits on an old volcano, and for centuries, carbon dioxide leaked into its deep water.
Then one night, it burst, like a shaken bottle.
The gas is heavier than air, so it rolled down into the valleys.
Pushed the oxygen away, and people in its path fell asleep and never woke up.
Today, pipes pump the gas out, so it can't happen again.
But two other lakes on Earth are known to hold gas like this.
